prize_parts.citation: For the prediction of flat bands in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene and the discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in it, opening the field of moire quantum materials

statement.case_for: B047 is what I would call a discovery-driven prize of the kind the committee can defend: a precise prediction (Bistritzer and MacDonald, flat bands at a magic twist angle) followed by an unambiguous experiment (Jarillo-Herrero and collaborators, 2018) that showed correlated insulating and superconducting states in a tunable two-dimensional system. It has been reproduced by many groups and carried across several moire platforms in under a decade. As a microscopist I value that the twist angle and local structure can be checked directly, so the physics is anchored in a controllable, measurable parameter. Opening support is also unusually broad: four top-three rankings and no member who regards it as outside the field.
statement.case_against: The mechanism of the superconductivity is still unresolved, and the field is young compared with the topological-insulator or lattice-clock candidates. Sample-to-sample variation in twist-angle disorder is real, and credit is not cleanly three-way: earlier moire band-structure theory and rapid parallel experiments elsewhere could be argued to dilute the attribution, and the Bistritzer and MacDonald paper is a theory prediction that preceded the experiment by seven years. If the committee wants a prize resting on settled interpretation, B012 is the safer choice.

responses.point: Mehlig ranks B047 second behind active-matter hydrodynamics (B009), but would credit mainly Jarillo-Herrero and MacDonald as a clean theory-plus-experiment pair, and worries that an unfinished understanding of the superconductivity sits uneasily with a discovery prize.
responses.response: I share the concern about the pairing mechanism, but the prize criterion is a discovery or invention, not a finished explanation; the flat-band prediction and the observed correlated phases are the discovery. I would keep Bistritzer, because the continuum-model prediction is what identified the magic angle, and removing him leaves the experiment without its theoretical origin. I do not see B009 as competing at this point: it has one supporter, and the quantitative confirmation of the Toner-Tu exponents in real systems is incomplete, as Mehlig himself notes.

responses.point: Eriksson places dynamical mean-field theory (B005) first as a systematically improvable framework with three decades of use, and ranks twisted bilayer graphene only fifth.
responses.response: DMFT is important and mature, but it is a method, and as Eriksson himself flags, Nobel practice for methods is uneven; the credit split between the infinite-dimension limit and the impurity mapping also leaves a name outside the supplied trio. B047 is a concrete discovery with a clear prediction-to-experiment chain. I accept his point that B047 is less mature, and I would weigh that in the final ballot, but I do not think it outweighs the cleaner attribution.

responses.point: Kroll puts optical lattice clocks (B019) first on the grounds of independent reproduction at the 10^-18 level in several countries and a clean two-person configuration, and ranks twisted bilayer graphene seventh.
responses.response: I take the maturity and attribution arguments for B019 seriously and keep it as an alternative, since Katori and Ye are an exemplary invention-plus-realisation pair. My reservation, which Kroll and Lindroth both mention, is the overlap with the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 ion-clock recognitions, which weakens novelty relative to a field that did not exist ten years ago. I disagree with ranking B047 that low on the ground of maturity alone: replication across many groups and platforms since 2018 is exactly the kind of confirmation the clock community points to.

responses.point: Danielsson ranks B047 first with the three credited names as a natural theory-plus-experiment trio, while noting that credit may be concentrated in one experimental group and that the pairing mechanism is open.
responses.response: I agree with the configuration and with the flagged uncertainties. On the experimental concentration, the 2018 pair of papers from one group are the decisive observations and the later work from other laboratories confirmed rather than preceded them, so I am comfortable with a single experimental laureate. I would like the committee to check the pre-2018 moire band-structure literature before the citation wording is fixed.

uncertainties: Whether the unresolved superconducting mechanism should delay recognition relative to the more settled B012 or B019.
Whether pre-2018 moire band-structure theory requires a different credited set or only a careful citation.
How much weight the committee gives to overlap with earlier prizes for B019 versus the youth of B047.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for B047, B012 or B019; my Chalmers colleague Goran Johansson ranks different candidates first and I have no documented tie to any credited name, though I note my Chalmers affiliation and microscopy network for completeness.
